problem: Consider the section of the parabola ${x}^{2}-4y=4$ that lies in the first quadrant.  Given that $x=x(t),$ $y=y(t),$  and that $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=3$ on the parabola at the point where $y=3,$ find the value of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}$ at that point.

feedback.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{9})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{9})-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (\frac{2x}{9})-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (\frac{2y}{9}) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=12$ and $x=-5,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}12\cdot (\frac{2(-5)}{9})-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (\frac{2y}{9}) & =0 \\ -\frac{120}{9}-\frac{2y}{9}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We also want to substitute for $y,$ but we are not given this value. However, we can find it by substituting $x=-5$ into the equation of the hyperbola.

At the point where $x=-5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{(-5)^{2}}{9}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{25}{9}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ 25-{y}^{2} & =9 \\ {y}^{2} & =16 \\ y & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used $y>0$ since we're only interested in the second quadrant.

Finally, substituting $y=4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{120}{9}-\frac{2(4)}{9}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0 \\ -\frac{120}{9}-\frac{8}{9}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0 \\ -\frac{8}{9}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{120}{9} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =-\frac{120}{8} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =-15.\end{aligned}
$$
